text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Many Norwegian researchers are dependent upon employers and adapt, to a large degree, results to match expectations, says Matthias Kaiser, leader of the national committee for research ethics.
- 120,000 six and seven-year-olds will begin school today for the first time under the country's reform for children to begin school earlier.
- Conservative party leader Jan Petersen says there is a theoretical possibility that he could become Norway's next prime minister although his party may do poorly in the September 15 election.

- Billionaire investor Kjell Inge Roekke accepts blame for the negative developments in Norway Seafood, which has taken a provision in the first half of the year of 400 million crowns for restructuring costs.

- Analysts say last week's historic plunge at Wall Street should not cause any panic at the Oslo Stock Exchange. Share prices are expected to feel the pinch but in the longer term the posititive trend will continue, they say.
- Norwegian Internet websites are dominated by information on next month's election.
